title: Jacob, Israel, and the Tabernacle of the Word
english: The beginning of his judgments: all those eating him shall be filled with calamity, evil or violence upon them, says the Lord.

Those about to eat the people of God unjustly did not call upon the Lord, thinking to carry out all things by their own power and to tyrannize the people of God. For if they had known that they received him through the judgment of God by sin, they would have feared even more, lest they should fall under the same judgment. Therefore it is said to them, having become more reckless than is proper: 'Though I was angry a little, they themselves pressed on to ving tyrannized the people of God unjustly, they fell into cowardice. Therefore one should not fear a coward; for fear is not [present], if having received those delivered by the judgment of God, they approached them humanely and gently. But since they did all things harshly and without mercy, having fallen into cowardice, they laid waste to others. And this has risen up.

'Since God is in the generation of the righteous,' you will say, 'a generation of the righteous,' meaning the harmony of the righteous deeds in which the righteous judge is found, or the concord of righteous men and the commonality toward the same end. For if where two or three gather at his assembly, the Lord is found present, how much more would a whole generation of the righteous be found? And those who fulfill the same mind and life, even if they become a generation in different times, after this it would be said that time has called them to this. One who is cowed by a fear that is not fear; and he who fears man and once simply those killing the body, but not being able to kill the soul. For it is said, 'But do not fear anyone other than God.'

In connection with this passion, the Lord reproves Jerusalem saying: 'Who has not been reverent toward a mortal man?' (Ps 13:7). But as for the captivity of the people, it must first be viewed, so that we may subsequently see its return. He who falls away through his own laziness from the doing of good is taken captive by the law of sin, so as to have the power of death under the tyrantically devouring devil. This one, having been found having surrendered to the enemies outside the fatherland (and this is the partaking of virtue), is called back.

The Lord is submissive to the manner of repentance and to the forgiveness of those who have previously sinned; and this is the redeeming of the captives and the turning back of the captivity. When this has been fulfilled by the Lord's cross, as the people believing from the nations have been redeemed, Jacob rejoices. The same, according to the underlying meaning, is Jacob through thought alone, discerning the difference. For if one, doing good things and working according to virtue, overcomes the passions and evils and the working evil powers as a conqueror of them, he is Jacob rejoicing; but if, after the practical life, having obtained a pure heart, he sees God, he is Israel, a mind seeing God. For he does not receive into the voice of the Greeks a divine joy, being rejoiced; no one is grieved to take from a parallel passage the 'Let him rejoice and let him be glad' to be said.

85 Ps 14,1 See if the one living according to the law, having become the pedagogue unto Christ, dwells as a sojourner in the tabernacle of the Lord, wandering around the tent of the testimony. But the one having hastened unto Christ, having adhered to the evangelical teaching, dwells in the holy spirit of God, not another, but of the Son of God, concerning which it was prophetically said: 'The light of the Lord shall appear.' Stand firm, if it be rightly understood: the holy light of God is the God the Word, and his tabernacle is what the man took up. And it is necessary to know beforehand according to the flesh Christ, if he is the only-begotten according to the Father. He who says, 'Even if we have known according to the flesh Christ, but now we know no longer,' who has seen his glory, the glory as the only-begotten from the Father, dwells in the tabernacle, no longer a sojourner but dwelling in the holy spirit of God. And to him it is said: 'Ascend upon a high light,' he who evangelizes Zion. Therefore, the prophet, seeking an equal, says of the one able to say, 'Our citizenship exists in the heavens' (Phil 3:20), asks of the one to whom the Lord answers: 'Going...'

86 Ps 14,3 The one being erased from the appointed things, being a lover of brothers and a companion, hastens to be wise, spending time with the wise, turning himself away from all the weakness of the foolish, lest he be known as one of them. If therefore he turns away from the bad ones, but has understanding with the good (for the wise are good ones).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Unshakable Foundation of the Saints
english: He does not accept reproach from those approaching him, those who always reproach those who have evils approaching them as if they were praising their neighbors and having good friends. To this, the speaker is indifferent: 'Walking in an unblemished way, it did not work for my benefit; speaking righteousness, it did not direct itself before my eyes' (Ps 14:4c).

And the word of an oath of a man is unsearchable, upon which the 'Yes, yes' and 'No, no' are confirmed. If even at times there is a need for God to be a witness to the word toward the 'No', he does this unpretentiously, just as the prophetic apostle leaves behind a pattern and a guide in the Epistles, who says: 'God is my witness, whom I serve in the gospel of his Son' (Luke 22:60); and 'No': 'I call God as witness upon my soul' (Acts 20:26); and again: 'God, who is over all, is my witness, I do not lie' (1 Tim 4:5). For this is an ungraspable faith; for an oath is nothing other than a word with God's witness, a thing being confirmed by God's witness. And however an oath may be held, it does not invalidate an oath to a neighbor.

And it is also to lend spiritually without offspring, as it is signified by what was said to the disciples of Jesus by the Teacher: 'And do not turn away from the one who wishes to borrow from you' (Luke 6:35). For how could anyone say this perceptibly to those saying, 'We have left all and followed you' (Matt 19:21), or those saying with boldness, 'Silver and gold I do not have' (Matt 19:24)? Since, therefore, to lend perceptibly to the saints (whenever it is said they do this) is described, it is necessary to take this spiritually; the one lending must take the intelligible teaching word instead of silver for the sake of gaining something corporeal. For if even those sowing spiritual things receive the fleshly [things] only to be fed (for worthy is the laborer of his food [Luke 10:7]), they do not lend in this way; for they do not receive silver according to the value of the logical [spiritual] things given, but the only food.

And he shall not be shaken forever, because he remained through life having steeled himself in virtues (Ps 14:5ab). For this is the same as what is said here: 'I shall not eat meat forever,' and 'He shall be your slave forever.' He who has heard the words of Jesus and has done them remains unshakeable forever.

For he possesses the houses of his own citizenship, which are named as those having their foundations laid upon Christ, called a rock. They are not as firm as those concerning whom Jesus says, 'Whoever believes in me shall live forever' (John 11:25). There are some such as are standing; and what the apostle writes concerning them: 'Having been founded and rooted in love' (Ephesians 3:17). If that which is not to be shaken for eternity shows a greater endurance of an age, similarly examine the one said: 'And everyone who lives and believes in me shall live forever' (John 11:25).

The saints, remaining unshakeable for eternity, will perfect their life, not being limited by time but remaining always; and this is a symbol of their pillar of victory (Ps 15:1a). And this 'pillar-writing' of David is a prefiguration of the psalm to be set forth. For the deeds of those being destroyed and no longer existing do not turn out to be such; nor do the deeds of sinners have the quality of not remaining. For it is said that the enjoyment of sin is temporary, and that the sin of the sinner and the evil one will not be found. But the life of the saints is not such; for they look toward the things not seen and eternal. It is said, therefore, concerning each of them: 'His righteousness remains for the age of ages.' And since it is called a pillar in another way, as scriptures elsewhere lay down laws calling them tablets and boards, it should be called a 'pillar-writing' of the saints, who have handed down teachings written not on stone tablets but on fleshly tablets, that is, having ears and hearts favorable and well-receiving toward the writing. How he possesses the things of the prefiguration of the psalm, we shall see when God reveals it.

Since I have put my hope in you, O Lord, protect me (Ps 15:1b). For I will not be able to endure harmlessly, with myriads of enemies both visible and invisible attacking. Having prayed these things, he brought forth: 'The Lord is my Lord' (Ps 16:2). Who, sinning, is able to confirm this with his voice? For a slave who makes himself a sinner cannot serve God; for no one, he says, can serve two masters (Matt 6:24). Let it be said also in another way regarding the matter at hand. The apostle writes: 'No one can say, Jesus is Lord, except in the Holy Spirit' (1 Cor 12:3), meaning to say this by deed and disposition. For if it were merely spoken, it would be true...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Spiritual Inheritance and the Measuring Line
english: It will not be so, with myriads of heretics and hypocrites saying it is mere utterance and not having the Holy Spirit of God. For the Savior himself says: 'Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord' (Matt 7:22); and I, he says, will confess to them, 'Depart from me, workers of iniquity, I never knew you' (Matt 7:23). And again: 'Why do you call me Lord, Lord, and do not do what I say?' (Luke 6:46). Therefore, the one saying 'Lord Jesus' in the Holy Spirit, not in mere utterance but in diligent work and true disposition, is truly a servant, just as when you hear with the apostles, 'You call me Lord and Teacher, and you say well, for I am so.'

Thus, the one announcing the foregone things by a practical and contemplative life has established an unshakeable pillar crying out, 'If you are my Lord' (Ps 15:2). And since you turn out to be my Lord, I offer you gifts from your own dogmas, not as to one in need; for they, as not having need of our good things, receive them in order to grant back something far more excessive and greater. And not only through things presented sensuously, but also through spiritual things must the voice be presented.

For we perform virtues, as we manage our own bodies through complete temperance. We are what God accepts, not for our own benefit, but as those who ask him to give us the good things from heaven; for for whose grace does God seek human virtue, if not so that he might grant higher things instead of those which we offer to him? The holy ones of God dwell upon his earth (Ps 15:3a). And this heavenly Jerusalem is that in which they have a citizenship in heaven, even as they dwell on earth.

He never says 'not to gather their assemblies,' but 'out of blood' (Ps 15:4bc); nor does he say 'not to remember their names,' but 'through my lips' (Ps 15:4bc). Perhaps, when there are some gathering assemblies out of blood, pouring them out to harm those gathered, he is himself benefiting, rather vivifying those who are called, gathering them not out of blood but out of immortality, remembering their characteristics, not out of superficiality but having depth of disposition. It will also be said thus: even if many prophets and apostles were killed, their blood being poured out, it is not in these many blood-offerings [that the truth lies].

I will gather the assemblies of them, but only into the one single eye of the spotless and unblemished Christ; for this honor is given, so that they might be liberated from their vain, ancestral conduct. Concerning those who have been thus liberated, he will remember not by word alone, but by deep insight. [Ps 15:5a] He who has become above all the world possesses no other portion and inheritance than God; for everyone must renounce all things, so that one might be able to say, 'My portion is God unto the age of ages.' And as for the seed of the inheritance, it is also the cup that brings joy to the righteous portion, the Lord.

It is worth observing how the Lord becomes a cup for someone. Never does he provide moral instruction and thereby nourish the man in secret, becoming bread, supporting the heart of the eater; but he is also a cup according to the theory of truth, providing joy to the one drinking through the agreement of the illumination of knowledge. This cup is provided by the true vine so that the mind might be made to drink and be made glad, as one might graciously say, 'Esau has taken joy into my heart.' [Ps 15:6] And you will understand thus: he who has God harmoniously and his [possessions] will enjoy.

For he who has the Lord as a portion of the inheritance and his [possessions] will enjoy, saying, 'You are the one restoring my inheritance to me'; but he does not restore this, saying, 'Come, inherit the kingdom prepared for you'; for if he is the same, [he says], 'My portion is in the land of the living.' Regarding this spiritual inheritance, given by analogy to faith and excellent life to the heirs, it is fitting that the measuring line fell upon me among the best; for the cord is a symbol of measure and lot.

Indeed, concerning the sensible earth, into which the Hebrews were led by Joshua the son of Nun, being divided, it has been written many times: 'And the cord fell upon the tribe of Judah, and upon Reuben, the other of the twelve, upon this climate, the eastern one, and another past this.' Having observed these things, he who says, 'The measuring line fell upon me among the best,' demonstrates that good things were distributed to him, having entered into the best parts of the inheritance, which his lot shows through these spiritual geometric cords.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
